notes: Read in full. Remarks are Smith's opinion and forecast, not research findings.
headline: Microsoft vice chair Brad Smith said the effect of AI on jobs could take up to 25 years to play out and that governments should prepare with skills training and new rules.
score_reason: Senior industry voice on jobs and regulation; an opinion and forecast, no change from pool score.
importance_line: Workers and governments are the audience; Smith says AI is not yet displacing many jobs, but this is the view of the head of a company that sells AI, not an independent measurement.
summary: The Irish Times reports that Brad Smith, vice chair and president of Microsoft, told its Inside Business podcast in Dublin that "so far we are not seeing AI displace a lot of jobs" but that its effects could take up to 25 years to play out and will need skills training and "creative Government policies". He also said there are "more safety rules for a carton of milk than for the most powerful AI on the planet", expects governments to move first on rules such as duties to report AI incidents, and cited Microsoft research ranking Ireland third in the world for share of people using generative AI.
